title: Coding-agent CLIs as the operator level
summary: Makes the coding-agent CLI session that already operates Agent Studio an explicit product level next to the in-app chat. Defines roles and identities (owner, in-app chat, operator agent, runners, review hosts) and what stays with the owner. Derives the operator surface from the working set of 1 to 3 November 2026 and names the gaps: a decision stream instead of polling, cross-project batch triage, continue with the result ref, a capacity view, deploy and restart preflight. Turns six guardrails into server-enforced rules, and shares context through the card timeline, a new operator log, Dossiers and an attention lease. Recommended: an official studio-op CLI over documented REST with one portable skill, an SSE decision stream with a watcher lease, an attention lease plus revision checks, and a narrow operator role now, mapped onto SM-1 later. The operator agent runs on its own subscription and routes model changes through central model selection (AGT-3459). Ten implementation cards and a website page outline. Evidence includes light and dark captures from a fresh networked monolith.

implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# Narrow operator role and token file convention

Source: docs/operator-agent-level/index.html (AGT-3462), decisions OA-D4. Read that Dossier and workbench.json first, then AGENTS.md, docs/start/contribution-and-style-guide.html, docs/operations/security/overview.md and docs/security-model/index.html. Use the Dossier's recommended option for each named decision unless a recorded operator decision selects another, and record in results/status.md which option you implemented.

Dependencies: none. Resolve card ids (OP-n, SM-n) to promoted task keys before starting dependent work.

Entry points: backend/Features/Security/Iam/LegacyRoleMapping.cs, Iam/AccessSecurityStore.Iam.cs (CreateApiToken), AccessSecurityMiddleware.AuthorizeServiceAccount, Settings > Access (features/access/components/access-service-accounts), .agents/skills/task-api/scripts/access.js.

## Deliver
Map the API token role `operator` to a new IAM role `operator-agent` instead of Admin. The role holds the permissions of the operator surface (board and card reads, lane moves, continue, steer, create, title, batch gate eject and close-now, quota and routing reads, review step model changes, deploy reads and stage deploys of gate-verified commits) and excludes secret writes and reads of secret values, production approvals, access administration and installation-wide settings. Migrate existing operator tokens to the new binding and record the migration in the IAM audit. Change the default expiry offered for operator tokens to 30 days (maximum stays 365). Show the role name in Settings > Access. In the task-api reference scripts, read the token from a file (default `~/.config/agent-studio/operator-token`, override `AGENT_STUDIO_API_TOKEN_FILE`), refuse a file readable by group or others, keep `AGENT_STUDIO_API_TOKEN` only as a deprecated fallback with a warning, and never print the token.

## Out of scope
The SM-1 operator-agent principal and sessions; standing grants (SM-4).

## Acceptance
- An operator token receives 403 for secret writes, secret value reads, production approval, access administration and installation-wide settings in tests, and 200 for every route in the Dossier's operator surface table that exists today.
- Existing operator tokens are migrated to the new role on start, and the IAM audit records one migration entry per token.
- The task-api scripts authenticate from a token file, refuse a group- or world-readable file with a named error, and no script output contains the token in a test that greps stdout and stderr.

## Verification and documentation
Reproduce the gap with a failing test before the fix. Build any credential-shaped test value at runtime; never write provider-shaped literals. Do not include real hostnames, addresses, account names or project data in code, tests, docs or commits; the repository is public. UI changes follow frontend/AGENTS.md and docs/quality/design/style-guide-hard-rules.md and need Playwright coverage with light and dark screenshots under results/. Source: docs/operator-agent-level/index.html (AGT-3462), decisions OA-D2. ## Deliver
Add `GET /api/operator/decisions?after=<cursor>` (snapshot) and `GET /api/operator/decisions/stream` (Server-Sent Events) readable by human sessions and operator tokens, filtered by the principal's project scope. Emit typed events from existing facts, not from new rules: `escalation.opened`, `human-review.ready`, `decision-card.opened`, `backend.stalled`, `progress.idle-with-ready`, `batch.red`, `batch.isolating`, `push.pending-overdue`, `quota.exhausted`, `quota.fallback-active`, `watcher.heartbeat`. Each event carries id, cursor, time, project, card key when relevant, reason, suggested operation names and evidence links. Add a watcher lease: `POST /api/operator/watcher/lease` grants one lease per installation with a heartbeat; a second request receives `409 watcher-active` with the holder and last heartbeat; `--take-over` semantics require an explicit flag and are audited. Transition rules stay in orchestration-decisions; this card only publishes facts.

## Out of scope
The CLI (OP-8); new detection rules.

## Acceptance
- In integration tests each listed event type is emitted within 10 seconds of the underlying fact.
- A client that disconnects and resumes with its last cursor receives every event emitted in between, and no duplicates.
- A second watcher lease request returns 409 `watcher-active` naming the holder; a take-over is recorded in the audit.
- A project-scoped token receives only events for its projects.
